verdict.rationale: Cline's own docs show natural-language troubleshooting: CLI examples such as "run tests and fix failures" and "fix the layout issue shown in @./screenshot.png", plus an agent that reacts live to terminal output and builds through natural conversation. Plan mode lets it read the codebase and discuss strategy without changing files, which supports diagnosis before any fix. missing for 10: a dedicated debugging/troubleshooting workflow doc (e.g., stack-trace or log analysis guidance), independent hands-on corroboration of debugging effectiveness.

support.subject: As a developer, I can debug issues and troubleshoot using natural-language queries

citations.quote: cline --auto-approve true "run tests and fix failures"
fix the layout issue shown in @./screenshot.png
Executes in your terminal and reacts to output as it appears. Long-running dev servers, tests, deploys, all handled live.
It can read and write files, run terminal commands, use a browser, and help you build features through natural conversation.
In this mode, Cline can read your codebase, run searches, and discuss strategy, but cannot modify any files or execute commands.
Coordinated multi-file changes with linter-aware fixes, diffs, checkpoints, and one-click undo on every step.
